t: The Saka were the eastern Scythians, Iranian-speaking horse nomads spread from the Aral Sea to the Altai and the Tarim Basin.
They formed many tribes rather than one state, fighting and serving Persia and resisting Alexander the Great.
Driven south by the Yuezhi in the 2nd century BCE, they founded Indo-Scythian kingdoms in Iran and India.
dyk: The Pazyryk tombs in the Altai, linked to the wider Saka-Scythian world, filled with ice soon after burial and so preserved the oldest known knotted pile carpet.
ev: Cyrus the Great dies fighting the Massagetae, according to Herodotus
Darius I captures the pointed-cap Saka chief Skunkha
Saka troops fight in the Persian centre at the Battle of Marathon
Alexander the Great defeats a Saka force at the Jaxartes
The Yuezhi drive the Saka from the Ili valley and Zhetysu
Saka warriors kill the Parthian king Phraates II
Mithridates II of Parthia subdues the Saka, many of whom settle in Sakastan

f.capital: None (nomadic); centres in Zhetysu and the Altai
